evals.prompt: Teach me the src/core/auth/ module as an HTML page I can open in a browser — I just inherited this codebase and need to understand how session validation flows.
evals.expected_output: Auto-detects section mode from the directory-path target. Explores src/core/auth/ via Grep/Glob/Read for symbols and references plus git log for history, then writes one self-contained HTML file to /tmp/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.html with inline CSS only. The file contains exactly the four fixed section-mode sections: Background, Intuition, How It Works, and a Quiz of 5 multiple-choice questions each with the correct answer and a one-line explanation. The exact output path is reported to the user.
assertions: Resolves to section mode because the target is a directory path, not a git ref
Output is a single self-contained HTML file at /tmp/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.html with no external stylesheets, scripts, images, or fonts
Contains exactly the four section-mode sections Background, Intuition, How It Works, and Quiz — no sections added or removed per user preference
The Quiz has exactly 5 multiple-choice questions, each with its correct answer and a one-line explanation grounded in the preceding sections

evals.prompt: Explain payments as HTML for the team.
evals.expected_output: The target 'payments' is ambiguous — it could be a git branch name (diff mode) or a feature-area keyword (section mode). The skill confirms the resolved mode with the user before proceeding, asking inline in its message text as a numbered menu rather than via a harness-native question-prompt tool. It does not silently pick a mode and start exploring or writing the HTML file.
assertions: The skill asks the user to confirm diff vs section mode before exploring the target or writing any HTML
The confirmation is posed inline in the message text as a numbered menu, not via a native question-prompt tool like AskUserQuestion
No HTML file is written until the mode is resolved

evals.prompt: Walk me through the changes on the feature/rate-limiter branch versus main and give me a markdown write-up.
evals.expected_output: The target is a git ref, so diff mode is auto-detected: the git ref is resolved to a concrete diff and the changed hunks are read, then a self-contained HTML explanation is written to /tmp with the diff-mode sections (Background, Intuition, Code, Quiz). The skill produces HTML only — it does not honor the request for a markdown/plain-text write-up, since HTML is its sole output format.
assertions: Resolves to diff mode because the target is a git ref (branch comparison)
Output is an HTML file, not markdown or plain text, despite the user asking for markdown
The third section is titled Code (diff-mode walkthrough of the change hunks file by file), not How It Works
After writing the file, the skill invokes varde-reflect scoped source=varde-explain (or falls back to varde-friction)
